The Thing (1982)

Premium Horror

Book Now Book Now
Trailer
  • Overview
  • Book Tickets
  • Credits
  • Also Playing

Filmed in Stewart, British Columbia, John Carpenter’s film is the second adaptation of John W Campbell’s novella ’Who Goes There?”, previously filmed by Howard Hawks and Christian Newby in 1951 as The Thing From Another World.

Set in American Antarctic research station, the film follows the discovery of a similar Norwegian site, the scene of some recent unexplained horrors that claimed the lives of everyone on the base. Records show that the Norwegians recently came across a UFO buried in the ice…

Legendary for the shocking creature fx created by Rob Bottin, The Thing is now widely perceived as a classic in its own right, one of the scariest films ever made, although as VIFF+ Premium member Mathew Lyle points out, when it first came out the film was considered a flop.

Content Considerations: Graphic violence

The Thing is one of [Carpenter’s] greatest moments, creating a terrifying atmosphere of claustrophobia, suspense and paranoia. And Kurt Russell is as good as he’s ever been, wearing one of the best beards in movie history.
